data.name: Ojal
data.gender_notes: Ojal is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Goddess Ojaswini, symbolizing strength and vitality
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Ojas’, which means ‘vital energy’ or ‘strength’, Ojal is a feminine name inspired by the Goddess Ojaswini. This divine figure is revered for her power and vitality, often invoked to strengthen the body and mind. In Hindu mythology, Ojaswini is also associated with wisdom and prosperity. The name Ojal carries the meaning “Goddess Ojaswini, symbolizing strength and vitality” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ojal usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess ojaswini, symbolizing strength and vitality and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes inner strength and divine blessings
data.etymology: Ojal belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess Ojaswini, symbolizing strength and vitality.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ojal total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Ojal: The name Ojal is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Oj' which means vital energy or life force. 'Al' in the name signifies 'Aatma' or the soul. Thus, Ojal represents the union of the vital energy and the soul, signifying a life filled with energy and spiritual awareness.

historical_references.reference: Ojal was a legendary king of the Haihayas in the 11th or 12th century CE in the central Indian region of Malwa. He is mentioned in the Prabandha Khanda of the 13th-century work Hari-Bhagavata Purana.
historical_references.context: Legendary king of the Haihayas in central Indian region of Malwa

historical_references.reference: Ojal is also mentioned in the 15th-century work Adipurana, which is the first epic of the Jaina tradition in the Prakrit language. He is described as a powerful king of the Malava country and a devotee of Mahavira.
historical_references.context: Powerful king of Malava country and a devotee of Mahavira in Jaina tradition

modern_usage.modern_context: The ancient Hindu name 'Ojal' is gaining popularity in modern times, especially in the contexts of Ayurvedic skincare and mental health & spirituality. On YouTube, there are several videos about Ojal-inspired skincare routines and Ayurvedic recipes using traditional herbs and ingredients. Blogs and websites have extensive articles on the benefits of Ojal for the skin and mind, highlighting its spiritual significance and relevance to modern wellness practices.
